notes: 'ṛṣitaṃ' is a corruption of likhitaṃ, and 'dvijavala' stands for dvijavara. The line 'halaḍa, kaśurī, kaḍavasī ... rāvakhaṃ' is a medical recipe (haritakī, kastūrī, vaṃśalocana, puṣkaramūla, etc.) and names no persons. The note about Jitāmitra Malla is added in a different hand: 'Jitāmitra Malla had this book made, at the time of Minister (pramāna) Bhāgīrāma.' It may be a later note of commission or ownership, so it is uncertain that Viśvanātha wrote for the king. The catalogue also lists Śrīnivāsa Malla (Patan), but he does not appear in the quoted colophon; in 1690 he was no longer reigning, so the catalogue field looks wrong. The place is not stated, though Bhaktapur is implied by Jitāmitra Malla. The weekday has not been checked against an ephemeris.
